name: Law
dimension: the legal relation the claim states

objects.label: Sources
objects.text: LA.O.A1 Sources

objects.label: Legislation
objects.text: LA.O.A1.1 Legislation — statutes and delegated legislation, valid when made by the procedure the system recognises.

objects.label: Case law
objects.text: LA.O.A1.2 Case law — precedent binds lower courts in common-law systems (stare decisis); its weight in civil-law systems is lower.

objects.label: Custom and tikanga
objects.text: LA.O.A1.3 Custom and tikanga — in New Zealand, the Supreme Court in Ellis v R (2022) held that tikanga Māori forms part of the common law, as a source to be applied with care (UNVERIFIED wording; Māori-led review required). The tikanga itself, as tradition-internal law, is owned by IK.

objects.label: International law
objects.text: LA.O.A1.4 International law — treaties and custom (ICJ Statute art. 38). Domestic effect depends on the system.

objects.label: Validity
objects.text: LA.O.A1.5 Validity — what makes a rule law in a system (for example Hart's rule of recognition). The concept analysis is PL; the claim that a rule is valid here is LA.

objects.label: Obligations
objects.text: LA.O.A2 Obligations

objects.label: Contract
objects.text: LA.O.A2.1 Contract — formation needs offer, acceptance, consideration (in common law) and intention to create legal relations.

objects.label: Property
objects.text: LA.O.A2.2 Property — title, possession, land registration (Torrens in NZ and Australia). Title to goods sold passes under the sale contract and the governing law, not under Incoterms.

objects.label: Trusts and equity
objects.text: LA.O.A2.3 Trusts and equity.

objects.label: Family and succession
objects.text: LA.O.A2.4 Family and succession.

objects.label: Tax duty
objects.text: LA.O.A2.5 Tax duty — the liability to pay, set by statute. Incidence is EC and computation is BU.

objects.label: Wrongs and remedies
objects.text: LA.O.A3 Wrongs and remedies

objects.label: Torts
objects.text: LA.O.A3.1 Torts — negligence requires a duty of care, breach, causation and damage. New Zealand's accident compensation scheme (ACC) bars most personal-injury suits.

objects.label: Crimes
objects.text: LA.O.A3.2 Crimes — liability needs the prohibited act and the fault element, unless the offence is strict.

objects.label: Remedies
objects.text: LA.O.A3.3 Remedies — damages, injunctions, specific performance, sentences.

objects.label: Public power
objects.text: LA.O.A4 Public power

objects.label: Constitutional law
objects.text: LA.O.A4.1 Constitutional law — New Zealand has no single entrenched constitution; it relies on statutes such as the Constitution Act 1986, conventions and Te Tiriti.

objects.label: Administrative law
objects.text: LA.O.A4.2 Administrative law — judicial review for illegality, irrationality and procedural impropriety.

objects.label: Human rights
objects.text: LA.O.A4.3 Human rights — NZ Bill of Rights Act 1990: rights may be subject to reasonable limits demonstrably justified in a free and democratic society (s 5).

objects.label: Te Tiriti o Waitangi
objects.text: LA.O.A4.4 Te Tiriti o Waitangi (1840) — its legal force depends on incorporation in statute. The Waitangi Tribunal (est. 1975) makes recommendations, mostly not binding.

objects.label: Forums and proof
objects.text: LA.O.A5 Forums and proof

objects.label: Jurisdiction and courts
objects.text: LA.O.A5.1 Jurisdiction and courts — which forum may hear a claim. The NZ Supreme Court replaced Privy Council appeals from 2004.

objects.label: Procedure
objects.text: LA.O.A5.2 Procedure — pleadings, appeal.

objects.label: Evidence and proof
objects.text: LA.O.A5.3 Evidence and standards of proof — beyond reasonable doubt in criminal cases; balance of probabilities in civil cases.

objects.label: Arbitration and ADR
objects.text: LA.O.A5.4 Arbitration and alternative dispute resolution — awards are enforceable under the New York Convention (1958) in contracting states.

warrants.standard: valid source under the system's recognition rule
warrants.defeaters: repeal, inconsistency with a higher source

warrants.standard: source plus argued interpretation before a court
the forum's own rules of procedure and evidence

sections.governing_thought:
Law is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges.
Its objects divide into five legal relations: sources, obligations, wrongs and remedies, public power, and forums and proof.
sections.key_line:
Dimension: **the legal relation the claim states.** Order: from validity to decision.
1. Sources
2. Obligations
3. Wrongs and remedies
4. Public power
5. Forums and proof

R7 repair: v1's "order a remedy" is now member 3, "Wrongs and remedies". v1's "constitute the forum" is member 5, "Forums and proof". All three places now list the same five members.

Every legal claim is indexed to a system and a date: "under New Zealand law at 2026". A claim without its system is not placeable.
sections.assignment_rules:
1. Place by the legal relation, indexed to a system and a date.
2. Incidence is economics; the duty is law.
3. What law is, as a concept, is PL; what is law in this system is LA.
4. A dated event in legal history is HI; the rule then in force is LA.
5. The political cause of a law is PO.
6. Tikanga as tradition is IK; tikanga as recognised by a state court is LA.
7. A proved fact is settled for the forum only (W10 does not travel).
